title: India Summons Air India CEO After Phuket Flight's Sudden Altitude Loss
excerpt: Civil aviation ministry calls in Campbell Wilson as pilot drug test results and Airbus specialists add new layers to the probe into last week's mid-air scare.
body:
• India's civil aviation ministry has summoned Air India CEO Campbell Wilson over the August 4 Phuket-Delhi flight that suddenly lost 300 feet of altitude mid-cruise, injuring 17 people.
  • The pilot-in-command's initial drug screening flagged for psychoactive substances; confirmatory lab results are pending, and both crew members have been grounded.
  • Airbus is sending specialists to assist the investigation as authorities examine the aircraft's flight data and cockpit voice recorders.

India's civil aviation ministry has summoned Air India CEO Campbell Wilson over the incident in which a Phuket-Delhi flight suddenly lost about 300 feet of altitude last week, a source with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Tuesday.

The summons marks a significant escalation in the government's response to the August 4 incident aboard flight AI2379, which injured 13 passengers and four crew members when the Airbus A320neo abruptly dropped during cruise altitude.

Pilot Drug Screening Raises Questions

The CEO's summoning follows a series of developments that have deepened scrutiny of the incident. On Sunday, the civil aviation ministry disclosed that the pilot-in-command returned an initial screening result for psychoactive substances during standard post-flight testing. Samples have been sent to a designated laboratory for confirmatory testing, with final results still pending.

https://x.com/htTweets/status/2087160161869959328

The ministry did not disclose what substance, if any, was indicated by the initial screening. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has taken both crew members off roster pending the outcome of the investigation.

"We are aware that a post-flight screening test was conducted on the pilots in accordance with applicable protocols. However, the results of the test have not been shared with Air India, and we are therefore not in a position to comment on any findings."

— Air India spokesperson

Airbus Sends Specialists

On Monday, European planemaker Airbus confirmed it was sending specialists to assist in the investigation, according to Reuters. The involvement of the aircraft manufacturer adds a technical dimension to the probe, which is examining both human and mechanical factors behind the sudden altitude loss.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=i4vb5TyUY2M

The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has classified the occurrence as a "serious incident" and is leading the investigation. Authorities secured the aircraft's Flight Data Recorder and Cockpit Voice Recorder on the day of the incident, and the A320neo has been moved to a separate hangar for inspection.

What Happened on August 4

Air India flight AI2379, an Airbus A320neo (registration VT-EXO), was carrying 137 passengers and eight crew members from Phuket to Delhi when it experienced a sudden loss of approximately 300 feet of altitude during cruise. Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu said the aircraft encountered severe turbulence for four to five minutes.

Passengers described being thrown into the ceiling and aisles during the drop. Thirteen passengers and four crew members were hospitalized upon the flight's safe landing in Delhi. All 13 passengers have since been discharged, but the four crew members — who sustained spinal injuries including damage near the tailbone and neck — remain under medical supervision.

Minister Naidu visited the injured crew at Fortis Hospital in Delhi on August 5 and praised their response. "I would like to thank them for the bravery they have shown. Even after the incident, they continued to provide all the assistance that was required to the passengers," he said, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

What's Next

The DGCA investigation is examining passenger accounts, crew statements, pilot inputs, and technical data from the flight recorders. The confirmatory drug test results for the pilot-in-command will be a key factor in determining the course of the probe.

The incident comes at a turbulent time for Air India. The Tata Group-owned carrier has not posted a profit since returning to private ownership in 2022 and recorded a record loss last fiscal year. Meanwhile, Reuters reported that incoming CEO Tewolde Gebremariam — the former Ethiopian Airlines chief announced as Wilson's replacement last week — will inherit safety and compliance as top priorities.

Minister Naidu has said the DGCA's findings will be made public only after the investigation establishes the facts.
nri_angle: Air India is India's flagship carrier and a primary airline for the Indian diaspora traveling between India and international destinations. Safety incidents on its routes directly affect NRI travelers.
